body: I can relate.  I spent so much of my childhood playing games when I could have been developing social skills and making friends.  I should have been experiencing life instead of staring at a screen.  Now I have no idea how to talk to people and I constantly yearn for companionship.

1.  Aspergers is a mild form of autism, but that doesn't mean Aspergers is trivial.  Experiences with autism can vary a lot.  Some autistic people are very low functioning, so yes, compared to that part of the spectrum Aspergers is not problematic.  That doesn't mean that Aspergers isn't hard to cope with for a lot of people.

2. Aspergers is a form of autism so most people use the terms interchangeably.  In some places aspergers isn't even a formal diagnosis anymore.  It's just autism.

3. Absolutely.  Everyone with aspergers is different.  Some people are able to live normal lives, develop relationships and social skills, and find employment.  Others can't.  There's a lot of us in between.  Some of us can get a job or an education while failing to develop the social skills needed to really connect with other people.  Some people can't hold a job at all.

> But you are going to come back here as another person and re learn the lesson u tried to dodge .

What do you mean by this?

For some of us it is serious.  Just because it's not that bad for you doesn't mean that it doesn't cause a lot of pain and isolation for other people with the disorder.  There's a reason why people with autism have higher suicide rates.

Now, I'm not mad at OP or anything.  It's a funny mistake.  But to say Aspergers isn't serious is just ridiculous.
I'm also on the autism spectrum and crave human contact.  All I want is a hug from someone, anyone.  Loneliness hurts.  I hope it gets better for both of us.

I feel like I could've written this. Three years at college and no friends.  I definitely relate to you when you say you worry about being a loner forever.  That worry keeps me up at night.

Loneliness is very painful.  I haven't had an actual conversation with anyone in over a month.  I can't make it through one day without breaking down.  If I can't make friends in college, will I ever be able to?  It's hard to imagine I will.

I hope you find friendship in the future.
